newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds close flat, await U.S. indicators.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds close flat, await U.S. indicators.

text.p: Argentine bonds closed around their opening levels Monday with very low volume and amid uncertainty about the imminent release of U.S. economic indicators.
"The market activity was fairly calm," a broker for a major foreign bank said. "It surprised me to see clients calling and asking about the outlook and saying they would rather wait."
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 fell $0.12 to close at 123.40, while the FRB Brady bond due 2005 shed 1/4 to 86-1/2.

The market is awaiting amid great uncertainty the release this week of the U.S. producer price index and unemployment data and next week's data on consumer prices. The Federal Reserve plans to meet at the end end of January.

"In the absence of any domestic news, the U.S. long bond rate is still a key factor for the local market," the broker said. Another dealer for a local bank said activity was very calm with no genuine client orders.
"It was a pure dealers' market," he said.
"There is a fair amount of cautiousness before the U.S. economic indicators release."
